cases.source_text:
The iterables are collected immediately rather than lazily, unless a
buffersize is specified to limit the number of submitted tasks whose
results have not yet been yielded. If the buffer is full, iteration over
the iterables pauses until a result is yielded from the buffer.

cases.html: The returned iterator raises a TimeoutError if __next__() is called and the result isn’t available after timeout seconds from the original call to Executor.map(). timeout can be an int or a float. If timeout is not specified or None, there is no limit to the wait time.
cases.source_text:
The returned iterator raises a TimeoutError
if __next__() is called and the result isn’t available
after timeout seconds from the original call to Executor.map().
timeout can be an int or a float.  If timeout is not specified or
None, there is no limit to the wait time.

cases.html: Use clone-on-write semantics with Arc::make_mut which provides efficient mutation without requiring interior mutability. This approach clones the data only when needed (when there are multiple references) and can be more efficient when mutations are infrequent.

needed (when there are multiple references) and can be more efficient when mutations

cases.html: Use Arc::get_mut when you know your Arc is not shared (has a reference count of 1), which provides direct mutable access to the inner value without any cloning.
